legend: Trotles is given a set of n%%ZSMJ0%% nodes and wants to construct a functional graph where the in-degree and out-degree of each node is 1%%ZSMJ1%%. Luckily for him, he is already given the some of the edges. For the rest of the edges he randomly chooses a node with the out-degree 0%%ZSMJ2%% and a node with in-degree 0%%ZSMJ3%% (they can be the same node) and draw an edge from the first one to the second one. Calculate the expected number of cycles in the graph modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ4%%.
input: The first line contain n%%ZSMJ5%% and m%%ZSMJ6%%, the number of nodes and the number of given edges respectively. 1≤m≤n≤105%%ZSMJ7%%
The next m%%ZSMJ8%% lines contain two numbers a%%ZSMJ9%% and b%%ZSMJ10%% which means that there is an edge drawn between nodes a%%ZSMJ11%% and b%%ZSMJ12%%. 1≤a,b≤n%%ZSMJ13%%
It is guaranteed that the in-degree and out-degree of each node given in the test case will be less than or equal to 1%%ZSMJ14%%.
output: Print a single integer representing the expected number of cycles.
If the number of cycles is pq%%ZSMJ15%% then print p \cdot q^{-1} \pmod {10^9 + 7}%%ZSMJ16%%.
